content: I am planning to formalize some basic properties of proximity spaces (sometimes also called nearness spaces). Is it likely that if I contribute this to Mathlib, it will be accepted? I don't know how often proximity spaces are met in university curriculums.
This topic was moved here from #lean4 > Will proximity spaces be included into Mathlib? by Michael Rothgang.
I have moved this topic to a more suitable place --- this will certainly increase your chances of a helpful reply. I cannot give you one; this is the first time I hear of that term.
Do you have an important theorem in mind that would motivate the definition?

No, I can't point a particular theorem. But I have written a 500-page book, whose main topics include "funcoids" introduced by me. Proximity spaces are a special case of funcoids (proximity spaces bijectively correspond to what I can reflexive, symmetric, and transitive funcoids). There are hundreds of theorems about funcoids. Now, my purpose is to formalize (and thus verify) my solution of the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem. Proximity spaces are used in the proof. Well, after a little thinking: I can use funcoids instead, without introducing the concept of proximity spaces. I started to actively use Lean, for verifying the Clay Math Problem.

I'd say this is not for Mathlib because it doesn't have enough mainstream applications yet, but you should rather develop that in your own repository. When you have shown its usefulness by proving an important theorem, we can reconsider the upstreaming question.

Also if you want a clear shot at convincing people, I recommend looking at FC#1457 whenever it lands, if you can produce a proof of the statement imported from this library -- that would probably go a very very long way.

If you can then also run it through comparator and lean4checker you'd really get people's attention. Good luck!
